about: Dated finds of Homo sapiens and its relatives, each as its source reports it, hand-curated for histeclipse. Dates are thousands of years ago; places are rounded to 0.1°. Where finds are argued over, competing claims share a question.

questions.title: When did our species first leave Africa?
When did our species reach Europe?
When did people first reach Australia?
When did people first reach the Americas?
When did Neanderthals and our species interbreed?

claims.claim: The oldest known fossils of our species, about 315,000 years old.
Omo I, the oldest Homo sapiens known from eastern Africa: at least 233,000 years old.

claims.question: first-out-of-africa
claims.claim: A skull fragment read as Homo sapiens, over 210,000 years old; the reading is disputed.

claims.question: first-out-of-africa
claims.claim: A modern human jaw, 177,000 to 194,000 years old.
Burials of early modern humans, about 92,000 years old.

claims.question: australia
claims.claim: Stone tools and pigments of people in northern Australia by about 65,000 years ago.

claims.question: australia
claims.claim: A review of the sites finds people reached Sahul (Australia and New Guinea joined by low seas) about 47,000 to 50,000 years ago, not earlier.

claims.question: europe
claims.claim: A child’s tooth and tools read as our species, about 54,000 years ago, between Neanderthal layers.

claims.question: europe
claims.claim: The oldest securely dated Homo sapiens remains in Europe, about 44,000 to 46,000 years old.
The genome of a man who lived about 45,000 years ago, with Neanderthal ancestry from an admixture not long before.

claims.question: americas
claims.claim: Human footprints dated to 21,000 to 23,000 years ago, during the Last Glacial Maximum; later dated again by other methods, with the same result.

source.citation: Bennett et al. 2021, Science; Pigati et al. 2023, Science

claims.question: americas
claims.claim: A camp about 14,500 years old, far south, before Clovis.

claims.question: americas
claims.claim: The Clovis culture, about 12,750 to 13,050 years ago; long held to be the first people in the Americas.
Neanderthals disappear from Europe about 39,000 to 41,000 years ago.

claims.question: neanderthal-admixture
claims.claim: From ancient and present-day genomes, one long period of mixing, about 43,500 to 50,500 years ago.
claims.wikipedia: Interbreeding between archaic and modern humans

claims.question: neanderthal-admixture
claims.claim: From the earliest modern human genomes, from Ranis and Zlatý kůň, about 45,000 to 49,000 years ago.
claims.wikipedia: Interbreeding between archaic and modern humans

claims.claim: Denisovans at the cave by about 200,000 years ago; the group is known mainly from its genome.
A Denisovan jaw at 3,280 m, at least 160,000 years old.
A molar most likely Denisovan, 131,000 to 164,000 years old.
